issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize both orders and the stock in the SealSaloon constructor, but later requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances) and final. Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is incorrect/confusing. This contradiction can lead students to either make stock an instance field (violating the 'static' requirement) or try to initialize a static final field in the constructor (which is not appropriate).
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement: specify that the orders array should be initialized in the constructor, while the shared stock must be declared static (and can be initialized at the point of declaration or in a static initializer). Remove or reword the sentence that says to initialize the stock in the instance constructor so students are not confused about static initialization.
